messages:
Anya: heads up — noticed a p99 spike (~2x) on the streaming endpoint after the kernel-routing change we merged last night. Repro on staging with 8k tokens shows long tails. :eyes:
Mike: ack. which routing change? the dynamic-kernel-selector that prefers fused-attn for seq<1024?
Anya: exactly that. Seems fine for median latency, but tail gets worse when microbatches combine long and short requests. profiling attached below.
Devon: can you paste the flame or perf numbers? curious if it's kernel switch overhead or KV cache eviction.
Anya: quick paste from perf-bot (staging, 8k load):
```
p50: 76ms
p95: 210ms -> 230ms (+10%)
p99: 520ms -> 1.05s (+100%)
Tail cause: 1) kernel switch path cost (65ms) when fused->unfused + 2) KV cache miss storm during truncation
```
Mike: hm that kernel path cost is the context-switch and JIT warmup for some kernels. We saw this in earlier experiments but it was masked by batching. If microbatch combines mixed seqs, we trigger recompile/slow path.
Sam: are we seeing a ton of microbatches that contain both short and long sequences? What's our microbatch sizing heuristic rn?
Anya: current heuristic: pack up to 32 requests or 512 total tokens, whichever first. That lets long requests push short ones into the same batch.
Lee: suggestion: introduce a tail-aware microbatch split — keep batches homogeneous by seq-length bucket for kernel selection. e.g., group seq<256, 256-1024, >1024. cheap to implement in router.
Devon: +1. Also, we should protect short requests from being stuck behind long ones by a max_wait millis for a batch (like 15ms). That reduces p99 for short seqs.
Mike: agree on both. But we also need a quick mitigation for production: propose temporary max_tokens cap per request to avoid extremely long generations causing KV pressure. e.g., enforce max_tokens_per_request=4096 for hosted tier until we ship batching fix.
Anya: can we test drop-in config change? If we flip max_tokens in config, latency spikes reduce quickly?
perf-bot: staging run after setting max_tokens_per_request=4096 and enabling seq-bucketing (experiment):
```
run-id: exp-189234
p50: 70ms
p95: 190ms
p99: 260ms
notes: p99 improvement mostly from reducing KV eviction churn and fewer kernel switches
```
Sam: nice. That suggests two root causes: (1) kernel selection churn when mixed-seq batches occur, (2) KV cache eviction policy causing cascading misses when long answers sweep cache.
Lee: on KV side, we should add eviction hysteresis + prefix-aware pinning for active sessions. Quick patch: hold a small LRU hotset of last 256 KVs for 30s, avoid evicting until we see sustained pressure. Reduced churn in perf run.
Devon: for long-term, we can also pre-warm alternative kernel paths for known frequent model shapes to cut the ~65ms switch cost. But that's a bigger engineering lift.
Mike: immediate action items: 1) rollout max_tokens cap to prod (hosted default 4096) as a soft limit with warning header; 2) enable seq-length bucketing router flag (opt-in) in Dedicated; 3) KV eviction hysteresis toggle; 4) follow-up for kernel pre-warm RFC.
Anya: I'll open the rollout PR for config flags and add a dashboard comparing p95/p99 by seq-bucket.
Sam: also add a temporary timeout policy for tails: if request exceeds 2x expected latency for bucket, return early with partial result and reason code "tail_protected" — avoids cascading backlog. We should expose this to SDKs.
Mike: be careful with partial results semantics and function-calling customers. Make it opt-in for now.
Anya: understood. I'll include opt-in header and a telemetry flag to track how often tail_protected triggers.
perf-bot: canary after rolling max_tokens cap to 20% of traffic:
```
canary-id: canary-189234-a
p99 (canary): 280ms
p99 (control): 520ms
error-rate: unchanged
```
Lee: looks good. If error-rate is stable and partial-results opt-in is safe, we can expand.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/seq-bucketing + config/max-tokens-cap -> canary cluster (timeout 30m).
Devon: follow-up: we should instrument per-batch kernel decision traces in the trace logs so we can correlate kernel flips to tail events. small change to runtime tracing.
Anya: i'll add tracing + dashboard. Also adding a short doc for prompt-limited customers explaining why we apply soft caps and offering Dedicated/private opt-outs.
Mike: thanks all. plan looks solid: short-term caps + hysteresis + bucketing; medium-term pre-warm and kernel-selection tuning; long-term QoS scheduling.
Sam: :thumbsup:  I'll coordinate SDK header changes for partial-results opt-in.
Anya: merging PRs today. will post follow-up metrics in ~1h.
